o: Rows must interleave female, other, male cyclically, with IDs within each gender ascending. Assign each gender-group a rank r (1st female, 2nd female, ...) via ROW_NUMBER; then global order is (r, gender priority female < other < male). In the example, ranks pair female{3,7,9}, other{1,2,6}, male{4,5,8} producing the shown interleaving.
k: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY user_id) gives the position within each gender block.
Order by (rank, FIELD(gender,'female','other','male')) to interleave correctly.

a.i: Rank users inside each gender, then sort globally by rank first and gender priority second — this naturally alternates the three genders while keeping IDs sorted within each.
s: CTE ranked: user_id, gender, rn = ROW_NUMBER partitioned by gender ordered by user_id.
Select from ranked ORDER BY rn, FIELD(gender, 'female', 'other', 'male').

c.python:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT user_id, gender,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY user_id) AS rn
  FROM Genders
)
SELECT user_id, gender
FROM ranked
ORDER BY rn, FIELD(gender, 'female', 'other', 'male');

a.t: O(N log N) — window computation plus final sort.

w: FIELD is MySQL-specific; portable alternatives are CASE WHEN gender='female' THEN 0 WHEN gender='other' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, or UNION ALL of three numbered branches. Pitfall: ordering by gender before rank (groups instead of interleaving). Follow-up: generalize to k categories with a configurable cycle order.
